what: Blur diet: no backdrop-filter below High Detail, plate tokens; at High Detail only .appnav .appbar .dialog__panel .drawer .popover__panel .page-header
method: scripts/render-harness.mjs, signed-in mock, headless Chrome on the lab PC (AMD iGPU), interleaved control (origin/main + #209) and this branch served from two builds; idle fps / scroll fps
findings: The unprefixed backdrop-filter before -webkit- in AppNav.css is dropped by the minifier; Chrome ignores -webkit-backdrop-filter, so Chrome has never blurred the navbar, scrolled navbar, bottom bar or mini bar.
Making the navbar blur work on Chrome at High Detail cost ~15 fps idle (140 -> 122-129), so it is deliberately not enabled.

On the emulated phone the gain is small or zero and the empty Dashboard mock is 15 % slower scroll without blur (not the universal selector, not skeleton shimmer; cause not found). Blur is cheap on this desktop GPU at phone size; a real phone GPU was not measured.
